subject: Talks focused on TMB at useR! 2018 conference

messages.author: cebb13ad16b3493f
messages.subject: Talks focused on TMB at useR! 2018 conference
parts:
I am wondering whether anyone is planning to present a TMB related talk at this year's R users conference in Brisbane, Australia, July 10-13? I am thinking of giving a presentation related to constrained optimisation using TMB and the nloptr package, but I don't know of any interesting content not related to my work. I would appreciate any suggestions if you think this is a worthwhile topic to talk about.

https://user2018.r-project.org/

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Talks focused on TMB at useR! 2018 conference
parts:
A TMB presentation at useR would be very good. Optimization with "nloptr" in combination of TMB (especially if you provide a TMB-based Jacobian for the constraints)
is powerful, and I think there are a lot of applicaitons for constrained optimization.

I can share some general TMB slides with you if you are interested.

messages.author: cebb13ad16b3493f
messages.subject: Re: Talks focused on TMB at useR! 2018 conference
parts:
I am thinking of submitting an abstract along the following lines:

In a recent and popular stats.stackexchange post, the following question was asked:

 

“I bet with my colleague that I will beat him in fifty consecutive ping pong games. So far I have won 15, what are my chances of winning the next 35 games?”

 

-- from https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/329521/

 

To answer this question, I model the OP (original poster) as a far superior player who still wishes to make the game fun for their opponent (they are colleagues after all). This leads to a regression problem for the OP’s probability of winning a point, that cannot be fit using standard regression packages. This talk will demonstrate how to use the Template Model Builder (TMB) package with an optimisation algorithm to find maximum likelihood estimates for the regression coefficients. It will also briefly touch upon the role of automatic differentiation in optimisation and C++ integration with R.


So no constrained optimisation and the dataset is small. But, with some thought in the next few months I might be able to simulate a dataset under a reasonable data generation process so that I can fit a constrained optimisation. Do you have any thoughts? Would you find such a talk interesting enough to attend?
